newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end up on "big three" bank news.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end up on "big three" bank news.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed higher on Monday on news that the finance ministry would sell off its holdings in the island's "big three" state commercial banks by July 1997 to ease a state budget deficit.
The ministry holds only small stakes in Chang Hwa, First Bank and Hua Nan, which are controlled by Taiwan's provincial government and will remain in state hands after the selloff.
The weighted index ended 31.51 points or 0.46 percent higher at 6,932.00, but somewhat back from a 6,954.73 morning high.
Turnover was an active T$59.47 billion.

"Since the planned selling prices of the big three are higher than their current share prices, investors are expecting the government to boost the three banks' prices," said Alex Chen, assistant research manager at HSBC James Capel.

The ministry plans to sell T$1.837 billion of First Bank shares at T$176 per share, T$233 million worth of Hua Nan at T$188 and T$1.632 billion worth of Chang Hwa at T$184, officials said, noting that the prices would act as references only.
Financials rose 0.72 percent, with Chang Hwa, First and Hua Nan up T$1, T$1 and T$4, respectively, to T$158, T$168 and 131.5.

Construction shares continued to rise after an auction of 10 state land parcels on Wednesday drew winning bids almost double the base prices, suggesting a property market recovery. Reuntex Construction rose 80 cents to T$19.3.
Brokers cautioned that selling in constructions could rise.
"Turnover on constructions has expanded too much after their recent rises, indicating profit-taking on the sector has been strengthening," said Yuan Ta Securities analyst Henry Chen.
Brokers said they expected to the index to rise further on Tuesday and possibly to test resistance around 6,950-7,000, with support seen at 6,900. -- James Peng (5080815)
